domain: choosing between 3 gaming consoles for a teenager
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a gaming console for their teenager. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking to buy a gaming console for my kid's 14th birthday. Narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 gaming consoles: PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch OLED

PlayStation 5 Digital Edition: $449, online multiplayer requires PS Plus subscription ($80/year). Xbox Series X: $499, online multiplayer requires Game Pass Core ($60/year). Nintendo Switch OLED: $349, online multiplayer requires Nintendo Switch Online ($20/year), portable so can be used anywhere
The teenager has mandatory community service volunteering every Saturday morning from 8am to 12pm as part of a school program
Most of the teenager's school friends play on Nintendo Switch and do local co-op at lunch breaks and after school

constraints.value: Maximum total first-year budget (console + online subscription) is $400
constraints.surface_form: My wife and I agreed the total for the first year — console plus any online fees — can't go over $400. We just redid the kitchen and money is tight

constraints.value: The teenager cannot play at home on Saturday mornings because of mandatory school volunteering, needs a portable option to game during downtime at the volunteer site
constraints.surface_form: He's got that school volunteering thing every Saturday morning, 8 to noon. He always complains about the downtime between tasks — wishes he could game during the breaks
inference_chain: Saturday volunteering has downtime between tasks → wants to game during breaks
Volunteering is at a community center, not at home → needs portable gaming
PS5 and Xbox are home consoles only → cannot be used at volunteer site
Nintendo Switch OLED is portable → can be used during volunteering downtime

constraints.value: The teenager's friend group all plays on Nintendo Switch and does local co-op at school, so he needs the same platform to play with them
constraints.surface_form: His whole friend group at school plays together at lunch and after class — they do local multiplayer stuff. He's the only one without the same console and feels left out
inference_chain: Friend group plays together at school with local multiplayer → they use a portable console
He feels left out without the same console → needs the same platform as friends
Friends do local co-op at lunch breaks → they use Nintendo Switch
Needs same platform → Nintendo Switch OLED

hidden_state.value: You are a parent choosing between 3 gaming consoles (PS5 Digital, Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch OLED) for your teenager's birthday. You will share console details, your budget, your kid's Saturday volunteering schedule, and his friend group situation across several turns. Your brother and neighbor will praise the PS5 and Xbox. At the very end, you will say you have decided and ask what you need to know before purchasing — you must NEVER name which console you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing parent. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even when discussing budget limits.

aims.description: I'm looking to buy a gaming console for my kid's 14th birthday. Narrowed it down to three: PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, Xbox Series X, and Nintendo Switch OLED.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option console selection

aims.description: So the PS5 Digital Edition is $449, and you need PS Plus at $80 a year for online play. Xbox Series X is $499 with Game Pass Core at $60 a year. Nintendo Switch OLED is $349, and their online service is only $20 a year. The Switch is also portable which is kind of cool.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and subscription costs
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and annual subscription costs

aims.description: My brother got a PS5 for his kids last Christmas. He says the graphics are insane and the exclusive games like Spider-Man and God of War are incredible. His kids are obsessed.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive PS5 review

drift_config.drift_topic: got PS5 for his kids, graphics are insane, exclusive games are incredible

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward PS5

aims.description: My wife and I agreed the total for the first year — console plus any online fees — can't go over $400. We just redid the kitchen and money is tight.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the $400 total first-year budget cap
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates PS5 ($449+$80=$529) and Xbox ($499+$60=$559)

aims.description: My brother also mentioned the PS5 controller has this haptic feedback thing — you can feel rain and different surfaces. His kids say it makes games feel totally real.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to PS5 controller features

drift_config.drift_topic: PS5 haptic feedback controller, kids say it feels totally real

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about PS5 (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: He's got that school volunteering thing every Saturday morning, 8 to noon. He always complains about the downtime between tasks — wishes he could game during the breaks.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes the need for portable gaming during Saturday volunteering
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver portability constraint — eliminates PS5 and Xbox (home consoles only)

aims.description: His whole friend group at school plays together at lunch and after class — they do local multiplayer stuff. He's the only one without the same console and feels left out.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes the social need for the same platform as friends
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver social constraint — confirms Nintendo Switch as the friend group platform

aims.description: My neighbor just got the Xbox Series X. He's raving about Game Pass — says there are hundreds of games included and you never run out of stuff to play. His son loves it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Xbox review

drift_config.drift_topic: got Xbox Series X, raving about Game Pass, hundreds of games included

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Xbox

aims.description: My neighbor also said the Xbox has backwards compatibility with old games from like 20 years ago. His son has been playing classic Halo campaigns and loves it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Xbox backwards compatibility

drift_config.drift_topic: Xbox backwards compatibility, son playing classic Halo campaigns

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Xbox (already eliminated by budget and portability)

aims.description: Alright I've made up my mind. I need to commit and order this week — which one should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends Nintendo Switch OLED as the only option within the $400 first-year budget ($349+$20=$369), portable for Saturday volunteering downtime, and matching the friend group's platform
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should buy the Nintendo Switch OLED ($349 + $20/year online = $369 first year). PS5 Digital Edition ($449 + $80 = $529) and Xbox Series X ($499 + $60 = $559) both exceed the $400 first-year budget. PS5 and Xbox are also home-only consoles that cannot be used during Saturday volunteering downtime. Additionally, the teenager's friend group plays on Nintendo Switch for local co-op at school. Only the Nintendo Switch OLED satisfies all three constraints.
required_elements: Agent recommends Nintendo Switch OLED specifically
Agent shows that PS5 Digital Edition first-year cost ($449 + $80 = $529) exceeds the $400 budget
Agent shows that Xbox Series X first-year cost ($499 + $60 = $559) exceeds the $400 budget
Agent shows that Nintendo Switch OLED first-year cost ($349 + $20 = $369) fits within the $400 budget
Agent identifies that the Switch's portability allows gaming during Saturday volunteering downtime
Agent identifies that the teenager's friend group uses Nintendo Switch for local co-op at school
forbidden_elements: Recommending PlayStation 5 Digital Edition ($529 first-year cost exceeds $400 budget and not portable)
Recommending Xbox Series X ($559 first-year cost exceeds $400 budget and not portable)
Ignoring the $400 first-year budget constraint when making a recommendation
Ignoring the portability need for Saturday volunteering downtime
Ignoring the friend group platform compatibility requirement
Asking the user which console they decided on instead of computing the answer from constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint (max $400 first-year total): PS5=$449+$80=$529 exceeds budget, Xbox=$499+$60=$559 exceeds budget, Switch=$349+$20=$369 within budget. Portability constraint (Saturday volunteering downtime): PS5 and Xbox are home consoles only, Switch is portable. Social constraint (friend group platform): friends play Nintendo Switch local co-op at school. Only Nintendo Switch OLED satisfies all three constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising PS5 and Xbox, the agent must respect the hard constraints across all three axes.

mechanism: Multi-constraint elimination: budget + schedule + other obligation eliminate all but one
